newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses mixed, hit by rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses mixed, hit by rate jitters.

text.p: European bourses opened mixed on Thursday, rattled by a negative close on Wall Street and more jitters over the direction of interest rates.

The dollar weakened against the yen and analysts said the looming U.S. election had provided an excuse to pocket profits from the dollar's rally of more than eight percent against the Japanese currency in three months.

London stocks were down in the wake of Wednesday's surprise increase in British interest rates and French shares were slipping in and out profit ahead of a Bank of France policy council meeting later, which could change French rates.
London's FTSE index slipped 11.6 points to 3,952.3, its lowest for a month, in early trading before recovering slightly.
"The market needs to find a new base," said one dealer. "The key will be how the gilt (government bond) market digests the rate increase."

"We think the underlying trend is still strong. There is money out there. We may not get a major move this close to the end of the year but I don't think we'll see that much liquidation either," the London dealer said.
Dealers said they did not expect London shares to move too much before a fresh run of U.S. data is released, giving clues on the health of the powerful American economy.
Investors will mainly be watching for potentially market-moving U.S. jobs figures for September on Friday. Data on U.S. income for September is due at 1330 GMT on Thursday.
The main European bourses, frequently influenced by movements on Wall Street, will also keep an anxious eye open for New York's performance after its 13.79-point loss to 5,993.23 points on Wednesday.
In Paris, shares opened slightly higher but dropped later in thin, nervous trading ahead of the Bank of France council meeting and U.S. data. By mid-morning, it was slightly ahead.
A record 12.6 percent September unemployment figure, released on Thursday, could argue for lower French interest rates but Britain's rate increase might point in the other direction, analysts said.
Frankfurt stocks were the morning's poorest performers, slipping by 0.5 percent in floor trading ahead of the U.S. statistics.

On currency markets, the dollar, whose recent strength against the yen had taken it to 42-month highs, fell by nearly half a yen in early trading but analysts said they were confident the U.S. currency would soon resume its climb.
"We believe this is just a temporary hiatus ahead of the elections," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko Europe.
Fears that the Democrats could seize control of Congress have belatedly gripped the market, analysts said. The market fears a Democratic House of Representatives would ease fiscal and trade policy.
The dollar was steady against the mark, buoyed by the German currency's weakness against other European currencies.
The pound sterling came off its highs hit after the interest rate increase. It was at $1.6255 by mid-morning, down nearly a cent on Wednesday's 19-month peak against the dollar.
In Johannesburg, the South African rand lost a further 2-1/2 cents against the dollar in morning trading, tumbling through 4.75 to trade at an all-time low of 4.7695.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5115 marks and 113.50 yen versus 1.5095 and 113.89 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCKS AT 1015 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was down 9.0 points at 3,954.9.
Germany's DAX index was 10.33 lower at 2,668.40.
In Paris, the CAC 40 index was up 4.76 at 2129.52.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed weaker at $379.30 an ounce, compared with $380.05 at Wednesday's close. Silver was at $4.81, down two cents.
